processing: Tender buds and the top young leaves, covered in white down, are made as a gongfu black tea: withered, rolled, fully oxidised and dried into curved strands.
harvest_season: Young buds and top leaves. The exact season varies by maker; tender pickings of this kind are usually spring tea.
appearance_dry: Gracefully curved strands, said to resemble mountain peaks, with golden tips.
appearance_wet: Typically soft reddish-brown buds and small leaves, as with other tender Dian Hong.
taste_profile: Soft and gentle, with honeyed grip and a slight tartness, warm spice, fruit, bread and chocolate on the nose, and a sweet finish.

brewing.notes: The tender leaf is easy to over-steep, so start short and lengthen slowly. It also works Western-style at about 2 g per 200 ml for 2 to 3 minutes.

vintage_note: Usually sold as a current-year tea, as is common for Dian Hong, with no vintage culture around it. Best in its first year or two, stored sealed and away from light and odours.
description:
Dian Hong Mao Feng takes the name of a downy-peak green tea style and applies it to Yunnan black tea: tender buds and top leaves, curved into little peaks and flecked with gold. In Russian it often goes by Красный Маофен or Ворсистые пики.

The white down on the fresh shoot is the starting point. Oxidation turns it golden, and the leaf is shaped into a curve during rolling and drying, which is what separates it from straight-needle Dian Hong.

The cup is gentle and amber, with fruit, bread and chocolate notes, a honeyed grip with a little tartness, and sweetness left at the end. It should not be harsh; if it is, the steep was too long or the water too hot.

Look for curved, even leaf with visible gold and ask for the county and the harvest. Mao Feng is a shape and grade name rather than a protected origin, so quality varies widely between makers.
history: Little is documented about when this style first appeared. It sits within Dian Hong, the Yunnan black tea first trial-made in 1938, and within the gongfu black tea group. No named creator or founding date is recorded for the Mao Feng shape.
